the cold-spraying process is able to deposit a coating onto an aluminium alloy, and the laser treatment is able to improve the tribological properties.

the study of a cold sprayed titanium coating to improve the tribological behaviour.

the development of a novel surface treatment for aluminium alloys, based on cold spray and laser treatment, which is able to improve the tribological behaviour and, consequently, the service life of the components.

the study of a novel approach to enhance the tribological properties and wear resistance of aluminium alloys, which is based on the deposition of a cold-sprayed titanium layer followed by a laser post treatment.

the cold-sprayed titanium coating, when post-treated by laser, can significantly improve the tribological behaviour, in terms of friction coefficient and mass loss, of AA2024.

the laser treatment of the titanium coating improves the tribological properties in terms of wear resistance and coefficient of friction, and it also changes the wear mechanism from adhesive to abrasive.

the laser-treated titanium coating can improve the tribological behaviour, in terms of friction coefficient and wear rate, of the AA20204 alloy.
the cold spray process can be considered a viable alternative to the traditional thermal spray process to deposit wear resistant coating onto aluminium alloys.
the laser treatment is a viable and effective technique to improve the tribological performance of the titanium coating.

a cold spray titanium coating can improve the wear properties of aluminium alloys and that laser treatments can be used to tailor the tribological behaviour.
